Loans to non-financial corporates began to pick up late last year. Foreign currency-denominated (FX) loans recently reached their nominal pre-pandemic levels and peso-denominated loans have recovered after stagnating for a year. Loans to households picked up earlier, led by public non-bank mortgage lending, which was almost unaffected by the pandemic.","locator":"page 12","attribution":"IMF Staff Report, Mexico 2022 Article IV Consultation","period_fit":"2020-2022","source_limitations":["Haver Analytics data; Dec 2019=100 baseline"],"question_ids":["5B.3","5B.6"],"verification_status":"accepted","verification_notes":[],"premium_verification_required":false},{"draft_id":"D0042","source_id":"MAC-010","claim":"The 2023 budget entailed no change in the tax code but highlighted continued efforts to reduce tax evasion and avoidance, with authorities projecting oil prices well below 2022 levels and expecting improved excise collections including from fuels.","claim_type":"observed_fact","polarity":"favorable","actor":"Mexican Ministry of Finance","action":"maintained tax code; continued anti-evasion efforts; projected improved excise collections","mechanism":"no tax code changes; continued tax evasion/avoidance reduction; oil price projections below 2022","outcome":"no change in tax code; expected improved excise collections; reduced tax evasion/avoidance efforts continued","dates":["2023 budget"],"quantities":[],"excerpt":"On the revenue side, the budget entails no change in the tax code but highlights continued efforts to reduce tax evasion and avoidance. The relatively high interest rate differential between Mexico and the U.S. has made holding peso assets more attractive, which has helped in containing upside risks to inflation.","locator":"page 22","attribution":"IMF staff analysis","period_fit":"2021-2022 period","source_limitations":[],"question_ids":["5B.3","5B.7"],"verification_status":"accepted","verification_notes":[],"premium_verification_required":false},{"draft_id":"D0051","source_id":"MAC-010","claim":"IMF staff recommended allowing peso depreciation to act as shock absorber in balance of payments weakening, given deep and liquid FX markets.","claim_type":"recommendation","polarity":"favorable","actor":"IMF staff","action":null,"mechanism":"peso depreciation as shock absorber; flexible exchange rate","outcome":"Recommended policy: allow depreciation; consider policy rate hikes for large shocks with inflation passthrough; temporary FX intervention possible for market illiquidity","dates":[],"quantities":[],"excerpt":"In the event of a weakening of the balance of payments, peso depreciation should be allowed to act as a shock absorber. Standard financial frictions underpinning concerns about depreciation generally are not relevant in Mexico's case. In particular, peso foreign exchange (FX) markets are deep and liquid.","locator":"page 22","attribution":"IMF staff","period_fit":"IMF 2022 assessment","source_limitations":["Recommendation rather than observed policy action"],"question_ids":["5B.3","5B.9"],"verification_status":"rejected","verification_notes":["Mechanism additions ('consider policy rate hikes for large shocks with inflation passthrough; temporary FX intervention possible for market illiquidity') are not supported by the cited excerpt. requires complex legal, regulatory, operational safeguards","dates":[],"quantities":[],"excerpt":"Additionally, Banxico has recently undertaken a plan to launch a central bank digital currency (CBDC).
